text:
maria: Alert - Hosted API p99 jump on /v1/generate in us-west-2 about 20m ago. p99 ~ 2.1s -> 6.8s. Anyone seeing this? :rotating_light:
kevin: I'm on it. Any deploys around that time?
ops-bot: deploy:service/runtime v1.42.3 -> v1.43.0 by @ci on 2334567400 :rocket:
sam: That deploy changed coalescer/batching defaults (max_wait_ms 3->8) and introduced a kernel selector tweak for mixed-precision models.
maria: Can someone grab flamegraph/traces from a hot host? pprof or jaeger.
olivia: grabbing traces from host gpu-uw2-11 now, uploading.
olivia: link: https://internal-artifacts/redwood/traces/2334567890/trace.html
kevin: quick look — many requests got split into tiny batches (1-2) around the spike window. Coalescer wait looks off.
sam: Also kernel selector favored the "fast_int8_smallseq" kernel for a subset of requests that suddenly had longer seqs -> kernel fallback and extra memcpy.
maria: That sounds like kernel mismatch + batch fragmentation. Could be noisy tenant causing seq-length shift.
kevin: Querying KV cache metrics for that shard. I see high eviction rate and KV misses beginning at 2334567000.
kevin: tenant-id: t-42 has a spike in long-context sessions (avg seq_len 153 -> 420).
sam: That will cause larger KV pages and cause cache pressure -> eviction -> more priming -> higher latency.
maria: Any recent model variants added for t-42?
sam: Yes, deployment of mix-variant 'mistral-lite-v2-compat' as opt-in for that customer at ~2334566600.
olivia: Profiling snippet from pprof (CPU):
```text
(pprof) top
60.2% runtime.kernel_select
12.5% batching.coalesce_wait
8.1% kvcache.lookup
5.3% memcpy_async
```
kevin: kernel_select taking majority is suspicious. The selector likely mispredicted based on the sample sequence-length distribution.
maria: Ops actionables: 1) throttle t-42 to stabilize KV pressure 2) revert coalescer wait to 3ms or force batch_min=4 3) pin kernel selector to conservative path for affected models 4) roll back model opt-in
kevin: I'm scaling up the affected pool by spinning 4 more hosts, and applying an emergency rate cap on t-42 (5rps).
ops-bot: rate_limit:update tenant=t-42 limit=5rps applied
sam: I pushed a hotfix that forces kernel selector to prefer "generic_fp16" for sequences > 256 on the canary ring. Will promote if green.
olivia: After rate cap and scale, p99 dropped to 2.4s within 6 minutes, p95 back to 1.1s.
maria: Nice. Can we get a regression bisect on the kernel selector change in v1.43.0? We need to know which commit exposed the misprediction.
sam: Starting git bisect across runtime/selector. Suspect commit 9a7f3b changed heuristics for mixed-precision scoring.
kevin: Follow-up: we found a tenant-side traffic pattern that sends alternating short/long queries causing batch fragmentation — coalescer's adaptive sampler didn't weight recent long queries enough.
maria: Proposal: add quick-escape rule in coalescer: if recent N requests in the last 100ms exceed median seq_len threshold, increase max_wait temporarily to avoid tiny batches.
sam: Also we should add histogram-based kernel selector feedback loop: observe actual seq_len at kernel entry and penalize mispredictions.
olivia: Filing follow-ups:
- perf: add unit test for sequence-length shift
- runtime: revert coalescer default to 3ms and add adaptive rule
- infra: add KV cache alert for eviction-rate > 800/min
kevin: I'll follow up with tenant success to discuss opt-in rollback with t-42.
maria: Postmortem later, but initial incident contained. Thanks all. :heart:
ops-bot: incident:2334567890 status=contained severity=sev2 duration=33m
maria: Adding short note: root cause = combination of model opt-in (longer seqs), kernel-selector heuristic change, and coalescer fragmentation + KV cache thrash on a noisy tenant.
